what_happened: Scene L7: dark-green sponge_8 on a beige counter, cutting_board_9 (handle slot) ~20 cm to the left, sink further left. Stage 0: fingers touched the sponge from 71 while still open and closed at ~104 (width 0.061); lifted 9 cm, tilted 8-13 deg, carried onto the board (stage 0 from 109). Stage 1: pressed on the board at 160-166 (counter 1); 166-207 it held the sponge pressed nearly in place (counter blind, finger_joint1 at its open limit). From ~200 it dragged the sponge toward the robot along the board (y -0.18 -> -0.37 m by 244). As it did, the sponge worked its way out of the fingers: the wrist view shows it sliding to the bottom edge of the gripper, and the width fell 0.056 -> 0.035-0.040 (208-238) as the fingers closed on its thin edge (counter 2 at 209). At 241-244 it slipped out completely, onto the board near the handle slot, and the fingers closed on nothing (width 0.001 until 800). The gripper never opened, so this was not a commanded release. The policy then retreated as if finished (eef > 15 cm at 259), raised the arm and turned away; it never went back to the sponge. Final 2 contacts, sweep 0.081.
causal_chain: grasp near the sponge's edge, tilted -> dragging it on the board pulled it out of the fingers 200-244 -> sponge dropped on the board at 244 with 2/5 contacts -> policy retreated with a closed, empty gripper and never re-grasped
self_recovery: none: no attempt to pick the sponge up again.
official_criterion_notes: Blind window 166-207 (finger-1 grasp test) during a near-stationary press; minor effect. During the slip (211-240) grasp was also False.

packet_facts: gripper close_events 233 width 0.002 on sponge, not lifted (the slip)
touch ends 241; sponge rests on board z +13.6 mm

uncertain_about: Whether the policy would have released here anyway: it retreated straight after the slip, much like the early releasers, so the scrub would probably have been short in any case.
